fixes.row: The wisdom of men and of the nations, “of this age”: boasted in, made foolish, brought to nothing, led astray
fixes.why: The row files Ezek 28:12-17 under human and national wisdom, which settles the reading the note says the page leaves open. The Berean has “a lament for the king of Tyre” at 28:12 and “full of wisdom and perfect in beauty”; conservative and Catholic/Orthodox readers take the lament past the king, and a placement here makes the human reading the page's own. The note's “readers part” sentence cannot undo the placement.
fixes.fix: Split 28:12-17 into its own row labelled in the text's words, e.g. “A lament “for the king of Tyre”: full of wisdom and perfect in beauty” (Ezek 28:12, 28:17), with the note setting out both readings. Keep 28:4-7 (the prince of Tyre's wealth and mind) in this row.

fixes.row: The wise in their own eyes, shrewd or skilled in evil; the wise confounded, made foolish, put to shame, passed over
fixes.why: “passed over” states a decision about persons that no verse in the row states. Matt 11:25 reads “You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children” (checked in the Berean), and the Reformed and Wesleyan readings of that verse differ; the label takes one side. A label says only what its verses say.
fixes.fix: Relabel to the verse's own words: “…put to shame; things hidden from them (Matt 11:25)”, and drop “passed over”. Keep the note's “the page does not say more”.

fixes.row: Wisdom and the law: the statutes, the commandments, the precepts
fixes.why: The Hebrew here is תּוֹרָה, which the note itself says is “instruction” and “teaching” as well as law. The label names only statutes, commandments and precepts, and the Prov 31:26 example reads “faithful instruction is on her tongue”, which the label does not show. Every example must show its label.
fixes.fix: Move Prov 31:26 out of this row (it already sits in “Wisdom in the mouth…”). Relabel the row “Wisdom and the law (torah): the statutes, the commandments, the precepts, instruction”, so the Hebrew sense is named in the label and not only in the note.

fixes.row: Be wise, grow wise, make wise: “become wise”, “wiser than all men”, “make you wise for salvation”
fixes.why: Exod 1:10 (“Come, let us deal shrewdly with them”) is Pharaoh's scheme against Israel, and the Berean's sense there is not “be wise”. Under a label that names only wisdom, a reader sees the oppressor's plotting filed as a positive gloss of the verb, and the row presents one sense of the word as its whole (rule 4). The example at Exod 1:10 does not show the label.
fixes.fix: Move Exod 1:10 into its own verb row, labelled from the verse, e.g. “Deal shrewdly, scheme: “Come, let us deal shrewdly with them” (Exod 1:10, Pharaoh against Israel)”, with the note that the Hebrew verb is the same as “become wise”. Keep the rest of the verb row under “Be wise, grow wise, make wise”.

fixes.row: Jesus and wisdom: He grew in it, is asked where He got it, is “greater than Solomon”, gives it; Christ “the wisdom of God”; the Lamb receives it
fixes.why: The second row, which is New Testament only, sits directly under the Proverbs 8 row, so the reading of Wisdom as Christ comes straight after the Hebrew text's own Wisdom and before the Hebrew rows (fear of the LORD, God's wisdom, the LORD gives wisdom). Rule 5 asks the Hebrew Scriptures to be heard on their own terms first. The row order is not neutral on the question the note says the page does not settle.
fixes.fix: Move the Jesus row after the Hebrew-led rows (after “The LORD gives wisdom” or “Wisdom and the fear of the LORD”), keeping row 1 where it is. This moves no verse and changes no label.

fixes.row: The wisdom of men and of the nations, “of this age”: boasted in, made foolish, brought to nothing, led astray
readers: all nine seats (a factual slip about where a verse is held)
fixes.why: The note says Jas 3:15 is set beside “the wisdom from above” “in the row on God's wisdom”, but Jas 3:15 is held in this row and only Jas 3:17 is in God's wisdom. The God's-wisdom note says the two stand in different rows, so the two notes contradict each other about the same verse.
fixes.fix: Replace the sentence with: “Jas 3:15 is here; Jas 3:17, “the wisdom from above”, is in the row on God's wisdom, and the two are kept apart.”

worker_points.point: 1. Row 1 and row 2, Wisdom personified: Prov 8:22-31 not listed; the note quotes 8:22 and 8:30.
worker_points.why: The note is accurate: Berean Prov 8:22 reads “The LORD created me as His first course”, and the interlinear glosses the verb as “possessed”. But the row stops at 8:12 and holds no verse from 8:13-31, which is Wisdom's own continuous speech, so the passage is cut apart (rule: anything that belongs together). Add the span as missing, not as a note quote.

worker_points.point: 2. Row 5, “a spirit of wisdom” and the Holy Spirit.
worker_points.why: The note keeps each verse as written and says the readings part on whether the phrase names the Holy Spirit or a gift; the Pentecostal gift question (1 Cor 12:8) is left open, not settled by the row.
The note says readers part on whether the lament speaks only of the king, yet the row files the lament under human wisdom, which decides it. See fix 1.

worker_points.point: 4. Row 17, Rev 13:18 and 17:9 with Daniel's wisdom.
worker_points.why: The label says only that the verses call for wisdom and the note says the page does not say what is to be understood; the verses are not read as an interpretation.

worker_points.point: 5. Row 3 and row 13, “the wisdom from above” (Jas 3:17) and “earthly, unspiritual, demonic” wisdom (Jas 3:15).
worker_points.why: The two rows are right to be apart, but row 13's note puts Jas 3:15 in the wrong row. See the note fix.
The label leaves out the Hebrew sense “instruction” that the note gives, and the Prov 31:26 example shows that sense. See fix 3.

worker_points.point: 7. Row 14, Ecclesiastes: both sides kept on purpose; Eccl 9:10 touches the death hub.
worker_points.why: Both sides are in the text and the note adds nothing; the Sheol verse is only quoted, not used.

worker_points.point: 8. Adjective, “God is called wise”; Isa 31:2 “He too is wise” left in Every other use.
worker_points.why: Three verses name God and the one that says only “He” is left out rather than filled in.

worker_points.point: 9. Skill versus wisdom (row 6 and the adjective's Skilled row).
worker_points.why: The note keeps the craft sense apart and says the page does not say whether it is one meaning or two; no seat of mine is shown a verdict on the question.

worker_points.point: 10. Adjective “wise in their own eyes”: Matt 11:25 in this row with “the page does not say more”.
worker_points.why: The note is right not to say more, but the row label “passed over” says more than the verse. See fix 2.

missing.what: Wisdom's own speech continues to Prov 8:31. The row holds 8:1, 8:11 and 8:12 and nothing from 8:13-31. The two verses the note quotes, 8:22 (“created me as His first course”) and 8:30 (“a skilled craftsman at His side”), sit in no row, so the speech the Eastern Orthodox and Catholic readers take most closely is only in a note.

examples_checked: 24 of 26 rows' examples show their label; the two that do not are the law row (Prov 31:26) and the verb row (Exod 1:10), both in the fixes above. All 26 rows' examples were read; the God's-wisdom-is-called-wise row has three verses, all shown.
summary: The hub is accurate to the Berean and its notes are careful, but it files three contested passages under labels that take a side: Ezek 28:12-17 under human wisdom, Matt 11:25 under “passed over”, and Exod 1:10's scheming under “be wise”. The Torah row's label also leaves out “instruction”, and the Prov 8:22-31 speech is cut apart and placed only in a note, so the hub should be fixed before it ships.
